headline: Trading and lending lift revenue; securities losses weigh
summary_short: JPMorgan earned $15.3B ($5.57 per share, +10% y/y) on managed revenue of $50.9B, up 8% y/y; excluding $658M of securities losses, EPS was $5.75 and ROTCE 21%.
summary_long: Managed revenue rose 8% y/y: net interest income hit $27.1B (+13%) and Markets revenue $10.3B (+15%, equities +49%). Expense rose 12% y/y to $27.3B on revenue-related compensation, front-office hiring, brokerage and marketing. Credit costs were $2.7B including a $539M net reserve build. Average loans rose 10% and deposits 8% y/y. CET1 was 13.9% (standardized). JPM paid $4.4B in dividends ($1.65/share). Outlook: fourth-quarter net interest income about $28B and adjusted expense about $27.5B; 2026 Card Services NCO rate about 3.2%.
confidence_notes: Source is the earnings presentation slides filed as an exhibit to the 8-K (the exhibit resolver found no EX-99.1 text). Revenue is on a managed (fully taxable-equivalent) basis; prior-period values and q/q, y/y percentages are derived from the slide's dollar changes. Reported EPS $5.57 includes $0.18 of net investment securities losses; the shard's $5.75 is the ex-item figure. Outlook items are company-stated in the slides but are not written to the shard guidance array (no sanctioned script).

drivers.explanation: Net interest income rose on higher deposit, Card and wholesale loan balances; Markets revenue rose 15% on equities; noninterest revenue was held back by $658M of net investment securities losses in Corporate.
Higher compensation including revenue-related pay and more front-office employees, plus higher brokerage and distribution fees, marketing and technology expense.
Revenue growth outpaced expense growth y/y and credit costs fell; net investment securities losses reduced net income by $498M after tax.
The securities losses cut EPS by $0.18; excluding them EPS was $5.75.
Net charge-offs were $2.2B, down $389M y/y, with a $539M net reserve build.
Net income grew 6% y/y with strength in Commercial & Investment Bank (net income +20%) and Consumer & Community Banking (+13%).
